anya: uploaded failing CSV + example generations: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/evals/1893456789/failures.csv
matt: can you paste a minimal repro? is this only quantized variant or the fp32 baseline too?
anya: quick repro below — quantized only. fp32 looks fine.
anya: ```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('redwood/open-7b')
print(tok.encode("The capital of France is"))
# -> [1, 234, 56, 78]  (example)

# quant runtime uses local_fast_tokenizer fallback: different ids
local_tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('/models/open-7b/local-tokenizer')
print(local_tok.encode("The capital of France is"))
# -> [101, 234, 56, 78]
``` 
anya: note the BOS id changed (1 vs 101) which shifts alignment and makes prompt prefix get dropped in our postprocess heuristics.
samir: that BOS mismatch would absolutely break our prompt-anchoring check. did the tokenizer packaging change in the quant pipeline recently?
lia: we relaxed the tokenizer pin in the infra image in commit 0f2a9c1 last week to pick up bugfixes. I suspect the fast tokenizer binary in the quant image replaced the HF python fallback.
matt: where in the harness do we assume stable BOS/EOS ids? sounds like a brittle equality check.
anya: postprocess has this bit: ```if not gen.startswith(prompt_prefix_token_ids): trim_prefix()``` — assumes token ids from tokenizer used at training time.
samir: fix options: 1) canonicalize tokenizers at eval time to the model's tokenizer (preferred) 2) change postprocess to compare string-normalized prefixes instead of raw ids 3) pin tokenizer version in quant image (short term)
lia: quick mitigation: pin tokenizer==0.14.2 in quant image and force use of huggingface python tokenizer. I'll open PR.
